Spot reduction—the idea that you can burn fat from a specific area (like your belly) by exercising only that area—is scientifically considered a myth. Doing hundreds of crunches will strengthen and hypertrophy the abdominal muscles underneath, but it will not directly melt away the layer of subcutaneous fat covering them.

To lose belly fat specifically, you need to create an overall caloric deficit through diet and general physical activity, which allows your body to access stored fat from all over, including the abdomen. While crunches improve core strength and muscle tone, they do not override the systemic nature of fat loss.
